title: Short-form inference improv playbook (sketch)
content:
Purpose:
This is a short-form, improv-friendly playbook for sellers and SEs to use when they have 3–8 minutes with an engineer/architect or 5–12 minutes in a discovery call. Not a full deck — think pocket-handbook + micro-scripts + 1-slide rebuttal frames.

Audience / When to use:
- Platform engineers and integration architects at midmarket/enterprise accounts
- Pre-demo discovery, discovery call follow-up, quick discovery in SDRs > AE handoffs
- When the buyer mentions latency, cost, or on-prem constraints and you need to move to a technical win quickly

One-line opener (30s):
"Redwood lets you run the same inference API across hosted, reserved, and private infra — so you can hit latency and cost targets without ripping out your app when you scale or go on-prem."

30s TL;DR bullets (for busy buyers):
- Unified runtime: same API, rolling model versions, consistent observability
- Cost levers: batching, prefix caching, quantization profiles — measurable token-unit impact
- Reliability: fallbacks by model variant/region + canary rollouts + SLA options for Dedicated
- Private options: VPC and on-prem packages with KMS/HSM integrations

3-min micro-demo script (SE friendly):
1) Setup (30s): "We’ll show a quick hosted call, then where you’d pin a model and enable a Dedicated pool or Private deployment — and fallback logic."
2) Live: run a short prompt (20–30 tokens) to show streaming and latency numbers. Call out token/second and observed p95.
3) Switch context: show Console -> routing rules -> model pin -> fallback policy (simulate a capacity event)
4) Wrap: "Same flow if you self-host Dedicated or run in your VPC; runtime and API remain identical."

Rapid objection responses (short scripts):
- "We already have a self-hosted model":
  "Great. Many customers use Redwood as their serving runtime — we help standardize model rollouts, autoscaling, and fallbacks so your infra team doesn’t have to babysit custom code."
- "Latency is non-negotiable":
  "Totally — we’ll recommend a Dedicated pool, model variant (lower-latency quant), and binding to region to hit p50/p95 targets. We can run a short PoC with your traffic profile to validate."
- "Concerned about cost":
  "We measure token economics and suggest batching/caching + model quant recommendations; typical wins in pilot: 20–50% per-token cost reduction without regression in output quality."
- "Security/compliance concerns for PII":
  "Private mode + customer-managed KMS + audit logs are standard. We can run an on-prem proof or VPC deployment and map controls to your SOC2/ISO gaps."

Quick decision tree (for the seller):
1) Customer wants sub-100ms for 128-token calls -> Recommend Dedicated + quant/shorter sequence variant + region affinity
2) Customer needs data residency or audit logs -> Suggest Private (VPC or on-prem package) + KMS mapping + SSO integration
3) High-throughput batch embeddings -> Suggest reserved capacity + autoscaling profile; consider batch windowing and KV caching

Micro-checklist for a 1-week pilot (mini-PoC):
- Goal definition: latency target, cost target, success metric (NPS/accuracy)
- Selected model(s) and pinning policy
- Ingest sample traffic and observed sequence length distribution (attach sample)
- Console access + one SE w/ low-level tracing for first 48 hours
- Rollback plan and canary threshold values

Examples (short case notes to reference):
- Retail commerce search: moved from CPU-hosted LLM to Redwood Dedicated + caching -> reduced avg latency 40% and per-query serving cost 32% in first month (internal playbook id: RP-ct-04).
- FinTech compliance pilot: Private deployment with HSM + audit logs; customer required per-request audit trail and we mapped to their SIEM in under 2 weeks.

Cheat card: suspicious signals and what to flag to SRE/SE
- High request variance (bursty): consider burst capacity + autoscale thresholds
- Long-tail sequences: recommend prefix caching and early-exit heuristics
- Model regression risk on rollout: require canary with golden prompt set and rollback on quality drop > 3%

What to demo if you only have 90s:
- Live a single short prompt, show response stream and token time, point to Console -> model pin -> route fallback snippet. Then call out next step: "15–30 min pilot setup"

Short battlecard facts (one-liners you can say quickly):
- "Same API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private" -> less dev debt during migrations.
- "Autoscaling with SLA-backed Dedicated" -> predictable latency under commit.
- "Smart routing + fallback" -> reduced downtime in regional outages.
- "Cost levers tie directly to rollout policies" -> measurable savings without losing quality.

Open questions / TODOs (notes-to-self):
- Add a one-slide micro-visual for "fallback flow" (console > route > model variant) — ask design for a tiny svg.
- Validate exact per-token percent ranges for 2–3 model families to use as seller evidence (task: PR-122 in repo).
- Compile 3 short customer quotes about cost wins (sales team to share).

Linked play artifacts (for follow-up):
- Detailed pilot checklist (confluence: INF-PILOT-CHECKLIST-2)
- Canary prompt set (github gist link placeholder)

Notes to seller (voice):
- Keep it human: tech buyers want predictable economics. Start with their most painful metric (latency or ops time).
- Use numbers: "we saw X% cost drop" is stronger than a general claim. Flag that numbers are pilot-specific.
- If pushed for security details, move to Private + KMS + audit artifacts rather than long architecture discussion on the spot.

Quick scripts (closing asks):
- 15-min pilot intro: "Can we schedule a 15-minute session where we run a short pilot on a small traffic sample and return metrics on p50/p95 and per-token cost?"
- 2-week pilot ask: "We’ll run a 2-week, low-effort pilot with one SE and an engineer on your side; goal: validate latency & cost with a simple canary — can we get access to a small sample of traffic?"

Versioning + status: draft. This is intentionally short and improv-focused. Aim: give sellers/SEs a light-weight pocket tool to win quick technical conversations.

Feedback log (for iteration):

End of sketch.
